title: Vet Center Eligibility Expansion Act
official_summary:
Vet Center Eligibility Expansion Act

This bill expands eligibility for readjustment counseling and related mental health services through Vet Centers to certain members of the Coast Guard, National Guard, and Reserves. Specifically, eligibility is expanded to include (1) members of the Coast Guard who participated in a drug interdiction operation; and (2) members of the National Guard or Reservists who were activated due to a national emergency or major disaster declared by the President, or responded to a disaster or civil disorder in a state. Vet Centers are community-based counseling centers that provide social and psychological services to eligible veterans, active duty service members, and their families.

The bill also requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to submit a plan to provide Vet Center services to veterans living in geographic areas where no Vet Center is located.

summary.headline: This 2020 law expands who can get counseling and mental health services at Vet Centers to some Coast Guard, National Guard, and Reserve members, and asks VA for a plan to reach veterans far from a Vet Center.
summary.what_it_does: Vet Centers are community counseling centers that offer social and psychological services. The law makes certain Coast Guard members eligible if they took part in a drug interdiction operation. It also makes certain National Guard and Reserve members eligible if they were activated for a national emergency or major disaster declared by the President, or if they responded to a disaster or civil disorder in a state. The law also requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to submit a plan for serving veterans who live in areas with no Vet Center.

who_it_affects.group: Coast Guard members who took part in drug interdiction operations
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for readjustment counseling and related mental health services at Vet Centers.

who_it_affects.group: National Guard and Reserve members activated for a presidentially declared national emergency or major disaster
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for Vet Center counseling and related mental health services.

who_it_affects.group: National Guard and Reserve members who responded to a disaster or civil disorder in a state
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for Vet Center counseling and related mental health services.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans living in areas with no Vet Center
who_it_affects.how: VA must submit a plan describing how it could provide Vet Center services to them.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate start date. The law was enacted on October 20, 2020.
